evidence: All five lesson objectives are covered: parallel lines, perpendicular lines, bisecting a line segment, constructing 90°, and constructing 60°.
The pack follows the same five-topic structure listed in the lesson plan, in the same order.
Each section opens with a definition and closes with practice questions that map directly to the stated objective.
objective_curriculum_alignment.rationale: The revision pack addresses every one of the five stated lesson objectives in order, with appropriate JSS1-level content for each. Nothing relevant is omitted and nothing outside the curriculum target is introduced.

evidence: The parallel-lines section specifies set square and ruler, matching the teacher's stated instructional materials and method.
The bisection and angle sections use compass-arc methods that mirror the teacher's step-by-step board constructions.

The pack is text-and-figure based rather than a hands-on follow-along activity, so the student-replication element of the lesson (students constructing alongside the teacher) is present only in the Practice items, not woven throughout the explanatory steps.
taught_lesson_alignment.rationale: The pack faithfully reproduces the teacher's sequence, tools, and construction methods. The slight gap is that the lesson centred on students replicating constructions step-by-step, whereas the pack's main body is explanatory text; the hands-on replication is deferred to brief practice questions rather than integrated at each step.

evidence: The bisection section correctly states that PQ meets AB at 90°, which is mathematically accurate.
The 60° section correctly attributes the angle to the equilateral-triangle property (all sides equal = all angles 60°), which is the standard JSS1 justification.
The 90° section correctly explains why a wider compass opening is needed (the same opening would reunite at C itself), showing no conceptual error.
scope_conceptual_correctness.rationale: All five constructions are described without mathematical or conceptual error, and the scope stays strictly within the lesson boundary — no topics beyond what was taught are introduced.

evidence: Each construction is broken into clearly numbered steps with plain language a JSS1 student can follow (e.g. 'Hold the ruler firmly', 'Keeping the same radius').
Figure references are numerous but the figures themselves are described only in italicised captions; a student working at home without actual diagrams may struggle to follow some steps.
The 'Check your work' section gives full worked answers, enabling genuine self-assessment — a highly useful feature for unsupervised home revision.
clarity_usefulness.rationale: The pack is well-structured, sequenced, and written in accessible language suitable for JSS1 learners. Its main limitation for home use is that the figures are described rather than drawn, which may reduce clarity for some steps; however the detailed written steps and self-check answers make it genuinely useful overall.
